environment.wall_timeout_scope: one wall-clock budget per case for each side; a side that exceeds it is killed (whole process group) and reported status=timeout

execution.note: subprocess = killable process with the shared wall timeout; injected = test-only in-process runner, no wall timeout

isolation.note: both tools get a throwaway HOME/HERMES_HOME/TMPDIR plus an environment with credential-, session-, cookie-, and proxy-shaped variables removed; this is not a filesystem or OS sandbox — a process can still read absolute paths outside the sandbox, so it is not credential-proof

billable_asr.note: extract.py's existing switch; a public comparison never invokes paid/key-consuming transcription

case_command_mapping.trailhead_question: killable worker subprocess -> search.execute_search(<case lane>) + extract.extract_hits
case_command_mapping.agent_reach: killable subprocess: case.agent_reach_command, e.g. youtube subtitle / v2ex node

methodology.timeout_rule: both sides get the same wall-clock budget per case and are killed with their process group when it expires; per-fetch overrides inside a tool cannot extend the case budget
methodology.evidence_rule: evidence_ok requires status=ok and cleaned (markup-stripped) text at or above the case floor. A login/verification wall or a nav-shell page is rejected. A payload that is more than half markup is rejected only while its cleaned text stays under 4x the floor; above that threshold a long page is accepted on cleaned text length alone, which measures that readable text came back — not relevance or content quality. Transcript cases additionally require transcript material
methodology.ranking_note: No aggregate winner is computed. Cases differ in scope, corpus, and access path; per-case outcomes are the only output.
methodology.cache_rule: each run uses a throwaway HOME/HERMES_HOME (cold); reuse a sandbox to measure a warm run, reported as run_kind=warm
limitations: One host, one moment: network conditions differ between runs and hosts.
Cleaned length is not quality; a long page can beat a short canonical answer.
Markup-heavy verdicts apply only to short payloads; a long page with heavy markup is still 'evidence' if its cleaned text clears the floor.
Question cases search the same lane on both sides, but result ranking still differs by engine.
Agent Reach cases run through its own backends (gh, yt-dlp, exa, ...), so upstream drift affects only that side.
Both sides get a throwaway HOME/config and a stripped environment, which is not a filesystem or OS sandbox and not proof that a readable credential outside the sandbox was unused.
Auth-shaped cases are skipped by default; with --include-auth they are unauthenticated attempts in an empty HOME, not authenticated comparisons, and no session or consent config is used.
A blocked/errored side is a real outcome for this case, not proof of general failure.
Markup stripping is heuristic; a page whose readable text is embedded in scripts may be undercounted.

summary.ranking_note: per-case outcomes only; no aggregate winner is computed from case counts, content length, or scope-mixed cases
